text: Ursula Andress makes a stunning entrance as the shell-gathering islander Honey Ryder, emerging from the Caribbean surf in a white bikini. Her role is largely decorative, serving as the quintessential exotic beauty who needs rescue from Dr. No's underground lair.

This bikini made me into a success. As a result of starring in Dr. No as the first Bond girl, I was given the freedom to pick my future roles and become financially independent in European and Hollywood cinema.

publication: Journal of British Cinema and Television
text: Honor Blackman brought mature professional agency to Pussy Galore, commanding her own squadron of pilots and utilizing martial arts against 007. Her character subverted early passive tropes, demonstrating operational competence and deciding the outcome of Fort Knox by switching the lethal nerve gas.

Fiona Volpe is a fierce, ruthless SPECTRE executioner on a motorcycle with rocket launchers. She overtly mocks James Bond's assumption that every woman will instantly switch allegiance to him upon being seduced.

Diana Rigg's portrayal of Tracy di Vicenzo represents a major high point for female agency in classic cinema. She is not merely Bond's equal in high-speed ice car racing and physical combat; she rescues Bond when he is cornered and provides the emotional backbone of the entire film.

I had already established my reputation in The Avengers and at the Royal Shakespeare Company. Bond was great fun and paid well, but my career continued in classical theater, television, and film because I was fundamentally a trained stage actress, not a model.

Major Anya Amasova, known as Agent Triple X, is the top Soviet operative assigned to match 007 step for step. She operates as Bond's professional peer, wielding high-tech gadgets and asserting cold intelligence parity throughout Egypt and the Mediterranean.

Lois Chiles portrays Dr. Holly Goodhead, combining the credentials of a NASA astrophysicist with undercover CIA field intelligence. She pilots the space shuttle and manually calculates trajectory coordinates to neutralize Drax's orbital nerve toxin globes.

Melina Havelock possesses a purely autonomous motive: executing vengeance against her parents' assassins with her crossbow. Bond repeatedly attempts to dissuade her from seeking revenge, but her narrative trajectory remains fiercely driven by her own family duty and archaeological expertise.

Grace Jones dominates the screen as May Day, an imposing physical force who lifts men over her head and parachutes off the Eiffel Tower. Her climactic sacrifice—hauling the nuclear detonator out of the flooded mine—provides the essential act that prevents the destruction of Silicon Valley.

Pam Bouvier is a tough ex-military pilot who carries a sawed-off shotgun in her purse and saves Bond's life during a barroom brawl. She handles heavy aircraft and tactical logistics throughout the rogue Isthmus City mission without flinching.

Natalya Simonova is the decisive narrative actor in GoldenEye. As a level-2 computer programmer, she alone understands the Severnaya satellite codes. In the climax, while Bond fights Trevelyan, Natalya hacks Boris's mainframe, forces the satellite to deorbit, and calls in military helicopter extraction.

Michelle Yeoh's Colonel Wai Lin represents the pinnacle of female operational equality in the franchise. A high-ranking Chinese intelligence operative, she performs jaw-dropping stunts, possesses superior reconnaissance technology, and fights shoulder-to-shoulder with 007 without ever becoming a damsel.

publication: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Interview
text: I was already an established action star in Hong Kong before Bond. Tomorrow Never Dies introduced me to global audiences and Hollywood producers, paving the path directly to Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Memoirs of a Geisha, and eventually Everything Everywhere All at Once.

Elektra King subverted 37 years of franchise structure by serving as the primary villain rather than a decorative accessory. She manipulates both MI6 and international terrorists, weaponizing her trauma to control the Baku pipeline network and nearly incinerating Istanbul with a nuclear submarine meltdown.

Coming off her Academy Award win for Monster's Ball, Halle Berry brings electric star power to NSA Agent Jinx. She dives off Cuban cliffs, infiltrates genetic clinics, and battles Miranda Frost with fencing blades inside a disintegrating Antonov cargo plane.

Eva Green's Vesper Lynd cuts Bond to the bone with sharp dialogue on the train to Montenegro. She is Bond's intellectual match, manages the 10-million-dollar stake with cool precision, and suffers deep psychological trauma in the stairwell fight before her tragic choice in Venice.

Camille Montes is notable for completely defying the conventional romantic bond. As a Bolivian operative driven by the murder of her family, she fights alongside Bond without ever sharing a romantic or sexual moment with him, departing at the end as an entirely autonomous operative.

Lashana Lynch's Nomi takes over the 007 moniker with cool efficiency. She pilots tactical aircraft, breaches Safin's biological weapons factory, and provides heavy covering fire while maintaining commanding banter with Daniel Craig's retiring Bond.

Ana de Armas steals the movie in her ten-minute Cuba sequence as Paloma. Claiming to only have three weeks of training, she dispenses with evening-gown stereotypes to take down entire squads of SPECTRE guards with precision marksmanship and martial arts flair.
